### Contact Details (e.g. Tox ID or email)

_No response_

### qTox Version

v1.18.3 (for windows, downloaded from the qtox releases page)

### Commit Hash

b7802b42dcf5f68474eb4d6db66c004e3ca50848

### Toxcore Version

0.2.20

### Qt Version

6.8 1

### Steps to reproduce

1. Answer an incoming voice-call, and speak to the other side.
2. Observe at the qtox audio/video tab that voice input is registered by qtox (volume meter moves when I speak, gain is at the middle, threshold is at 0).

Note that sometimes I change the default system audio output device between calls (between HDMI out, and audio-jack-headphones-output), however:
- I don't change it during a call, and I don't change it during ringing before accepting it.
- Regardless of the system default audio output device, the configured qtox input/output devices are fixed, and are always available and working (specifically, laptop microphopne as input, headphones audio-jack-out for output).


### Observed Behavior

Actual result: I can see incoming network traffic, and I can hear the other side, but they don't hear me, and I don't see any meaningful change in outgoing network traffic, i.e. most network activity is incoming.

Typically, then disconnecting the call and starting a new call (even if the same way - the other side initiate a new call and I answer, without any system or qtox audio config changes), then it's working again - we can both hear eachother, and the network monitor shows roughly equal incoming/outgoing network traffic.

Looking at the log, it seems that audio-input failed to register by qtox when I first accepted the talk - eventhoug the audio/video tab shows the volume meter moving when I speak.

So there appears to be some diversion between what the audio/video volume meter shows, and what qtox actually tries to use for the call.

As a side note, it could be useful to display some very visible notification at the talk window if one of the audio devices failed to register. At least this would allow the the side with an audio issue to identify it early, and maybe even a "reinit audio" button if init failed.


### Expected Behavior

Expected result: other side can hear me on first attempt, and I can see outgoing network traffic during the call.

### Reproducibility

Sometimes

### Operating System

Windows

### Operating System version/distro/name/etc.

10
